page: Amazon Web Services c8i.large is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 4.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache resources consist of 48 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and a large 480 MB L3 cache. There is no local storage or GPU bundled with this instance, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a strong single-core performance profile, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2175.0 and strong single-threaded gzip compression at 34.3 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.34 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory-bound performance is limited. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is categorized as poor, and the Geekbench multi-core score of 2747.0 is weak. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with uncached large-block read speeds at 22.25 GB/sec and write speeds at 17.89 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c8i.large offers a modern DDR5 memory subsystem and advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) at an entry-level compute-optimized tier. The primary tradeoff is the low resource density of 2 vCPUs and 4 GB of RAM, which limits its capability in parallel processing, software compilation, and database operations, as evidenced by weak Passmark database and CPU physics scores.

This instance is best suited for single-threaded or light compute tasks, basic text processing, and lightweight utility services. It is not recommended for memory-intensive databases, heavy multi-threaded applications, or large-scale LLM inference.
